findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

Over 13 gnats were observed in the storage hallway off of the kitchen. They appeared to be focused around the raw onions and investigation showed a couple of the onions were rotten. The PIC was shown and the onions discarded during the inspection. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure that the flies are removed from the facility. The PIC was instructed to use their pest control to ensure that this happens. Ensure that the facility is maintained free of pests at all times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The CFPM available during the inspection did not have a completed allergen training certificate available during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all CFPMs have a completed allergen training certificates at all times. Complete the training and certification prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the facility could not produce their reporting agreements (from a previous inspection) or similar paperwork. Fresh copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements were given to the facility and signed during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all needed paperwork is available at all times in the facility.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD (RTE) with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

An employee was observed chopping lettuce that was intended for use in salads while using their bare hands to hold it. Education was conducted and gloves donned to correct. Ensure that all RTE foods are not handled with bare hands throughout the preparation process.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The blade of the can opener in the kitchen was observed soiled during the inspection. An employee stated that the can opener had not been used yet today, indicating that the blade was soiled prior and not correctly cleaned at the end of the day. The employee moved the item to dish for immediate cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned regularly and at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The insides of the standing freezer as well as the chest freezer in the back area were observed soiled with chicken juice. The equipment also has significant frost accumulation. The PIC is instructed to clean these locations and maintain them clean at all times moving forward.

(C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. 

Duck tape is being used to hold the central pole of the door frame together of the standing cooler across from the dish machine in the kitchen. The situation was discussed with the PIC. findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival sani bucket were not prepared in the facility. Once employees noticed the inspector’s arrival they went and prepared the two normal sani buckets in the kitchen. Significant food preparation and handling were observed to have taken place prior to the inspector’s arrival. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were made aware that they sani buckets should be ready for use at any time that foods are being handled.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Food handler certificates were not available for observation during this inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that food handler cards are maintained at the facility at all times. Inspector suggests placing them in the same binder as the reporting agreements, Norovirus clean up procedures and employee sick policy.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

A wet wiping cloth is observed on the counter across from the dish machine. Another cloth was observed on the counter by the drink station. PIC consulted and the cloths were moved to correct. Ensure that cloths used for wiping counters/surfaces are stored between uses in sanitizer solution.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Two containers of rice and two containers of chicken observed covered, and in the lower part of the prep cooler. Rice is 105F and chicken is 100F, both probed. Employee stated that both were removed from heat about two hours ago. CORRECTED- Discussed cooling methods with employee and PIC. Explained the need to monitor foods as they cool to ensure they move through the danger zone quickly. Foods were moved to shallow pans to cool more effectively.

(Pf)

findings.comment: Observed beef cooling in a cylinder container in the prep cooler without the time cooling began recorded anywhere. CORRECTED- Employee stated that it had been cooling since 12:30, and noted that time on the container.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Observed Cl sanitizer bucket at a concentration that bleached out inspector's test strips. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Sanitizer was remade to a safe concentration.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940
Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface
sanitizing solutions). (P)

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed container of tofu stacked on top of another, so that the bottom of one container is in contact with the food in the other container. Prevent contamination of foods during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. (C)

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed in-use scoops improperly stored with handles touching the food (peanuts, sugar, red pepper flakes on the cook line). Also observed bowls being used as scoops in bulk food storage. Use scoops with handles so they may be stored with the handle extending out of the food to prevent bare hand contact with food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12 During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) In the FOOD with their handles above the top of the FOOD and the container; (B) In FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD with their handles above the top of the FOOD within containers or EQUIPMENT that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon. (C)

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
CFM has not completed ANSI-approved allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. (C)

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Observed an open bottle of water on top of prep cooler in kitchen. Moved during inspection. Cease storing opened containers on top of food and food equipment. Provide designated area for drinking.  Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee go between general tasks and food prep, and handle raw, ready-to-be-cooked food without washing hands. In general, observed no handwashing on the cookline throughout inspection. See violation #10, no paper towels were present. Hands must be washed prior to working with food and when going between tasks. Discussed handwashing with PIC.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. (P)

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Observed employee touch raw shrimp with bare hands. Employee then proceeded to handle raw, ready-to-be-cooked celery and asparagus. Employees must minimize bare hand contact with food. Discussed glove use with PIC.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form. (Pf)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12  (Pf) Disposable paper towels not provided at either of two available handsinks in the kitchen. Provided during the inspection. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11  (P) Observed chicken, shrimp, and beef being stored on three shelves within the kitchen double door cooler intermixed. Chicken was moved to the bottom shelf, beef in the middle, and shrimp to the top shelf. Store raw meats so they are protected from cross-contamination. Observed ice bin in the wait station to be uncovered. Lid was replaced to prevent contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

Observed metal containers of food stored directly on top of other, uncovered foods. Ensure food storage is done in such a way that prevents contamination.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 FOOD shall only contact surfaces of (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified
under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code. (P)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Can opener is not clean to sight and touch. Can opener was sent to be cleaned and sanitized. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Observed the following foods, probed: fried rice at 90F in reach-in cooler; fried rice at 124F on the counter by the cook line; general tso's at 90F in the back room cooler; pork at 66F in the prep cooler. All items were in covered containers deeper than 4 inches without time noted when the cooling process began. Discussed active cooling and use of Time as a Public Health Control. Foods were uncovered, time noted, and placed in coolers.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed multiple foods in the prep cooler to be out of temperature (pork at 45F; raw shrimp at 50F; pineapple at 47F; tofu at 45F). Cooler was turned down and it is suggested that the lid is kept shut to help retain cold air.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained (2) At 5ºC (41ºF) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (C) Observed multiple foods (white rice, General Tso's, fried rice) at temperatures ranging from 90F to 124F. All foods are observed stacked high within deep pans and covered. No time is being indicated on any container. During the inspection, foods intended for future use were placed onto baking sheets/shallow pans, with time, and returned to the cooler. All foods appear to have been created around 1:30pm, so most cooling just had to be expediated. Bulk rice that did not meet time/temperature benchmarks is going to be held using time as control. The facility is in the habit of creating small portions multiple times throughout the day. Cease trying to cool these foods and simply counter hold for four hours then discard.  Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.comment: Observed employee go from working with dish machine to food prep without changing gloves or washing hands. Discussed glove use with PIC. Gloves must be changed and hands washed when changing tasks.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.15 (A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. (P)

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed several broken or damaged colanders, one blue/white, and one red. Replace damaged colanders. Food contact surfaces must be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11 (A) Multiuse FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be (1) SMOOTH and (2) Free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections; (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Facility does not have test strips for bleach sanitizer. Inspector provided a few test strips, but facility needs to order more.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Wet mop head is observed stored on floor by back door. Invert to allow for drip dry. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: CFM does not have allergen training. Take online ANSI-accredited allergen awareness class. Reference PA 100-0367 Sec. 3.07 (b)

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed covered, cooling foods without a proper label/no time on multiple containers of noodles and rices in the facility. Cease covering foods while they are cooling. Indicate the time on cooling foods. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed the can opener to be thickly coated with food debris. Also, observed the blender to be soiled with food from previous use. Pulled for cleaning during the inspection. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a No handwashing was observed by employees. Tasks changed from handling raw chicken, cooked noodles, clean equipment, soiled pans, and the dish machine. Handwashing was emphasized during the inspection. Gloves were also observed being donned without prior handwashing. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a Several metal lids are observed being used to hold vegetables as they are being prepared. The metal lids are crumbled and cracked to the point they are no longer able to be properly cleaned. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 Dish machine is not observed operational. Operator was able to correct the problem during the inspection. Machine tested at 100ppm Cl.   All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Did not observe a sani-bucket available for wet wiping cloths. Cloths are observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the dish machine to be thickly coated with food debris. Also, observed knives being stored beneath the island counter to be soiled with splash. Remove knives for proper cleaning. Scrub the dish machine between uses to insure grease and food debris is eliminated.   To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed horizontal surfaces within the kitchen to be soiled from grease and food debris. Island counter shelving, counter holding handsink, interior of upright coolers, and prep cooler are observed soiled. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Grey tub holding clean knives on the island cooler and dry storage shelving by back door is observed soiled with food Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: 750-1030 The faucet is not secured to the sink. The faucet will easily fall off the fixture resulting in pressurized water shooting up. Neck was secured during the inspection. See that the faucet is properly repaired so proper handwashing may be completed.   Water under pressure at the required temperature shall be provided to all fixtures and equipment that use water.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) Black mop water is observed within the bucket. Empty waste water after use. Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(b) Tools and mesh scrubbers are observed within the basin of the handsink. Emptied the sink during the inspection. See violation #12.  Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Screen on the back door is neither self-closing, tight-fitting, nor is it in good repair. Solid exterior door was closed during the inspection. Repair the screen door should you intend to continue using the egress. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Flooring throughout the kitchen is observed thickly coated with grease and food debris along the floor-to-wall joint.  Pay attention to floor beneath the dish machine drain board. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed wall by the prep cooler and the hood to be soiled with grease and food debris.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed a single service cup with lemons in it to be being stored in the ice at the server's station. Facility was educated on the potential for cross contamination with this practice. Cup was removed from the ice. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a laddle being used with a handle that was mostly destroyed. It was not smooth, nor easily cleanable. Laddle was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that non-food surfaces are maintained smooth and easily cleanable. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed raw chicken thawing on a clean dish rack. Ensure that PHFs are thawed in one of the methods listed below. Chicken was moved to the cooler.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed raw chicken being stored over clean dishes on the clean dish rack. 2) Observed noodles being stored on the surface next to the dish machine where the clean dishes come out. 3) Observed the same dish surface being used for other prep of noodles. Ensure that all dishes, clean dish surfaces, and areas around the dish machine are protected from cross contamination. Food should not be prepared in these areas as it poses a risk to contaminate the food. 4) Observed raw beef being stored on top of raw chicken and other raw meats with no separation. Ensure that raw meats are stored in the proper storage order and also not contacting each other. The meats were thawing in a cooler, but were not completely thawed. They were also wrapped in plastic. The facility was allowed to retain the meats, however, they were required to rearrange the cooler into the proper storage order. 
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed two instances where ice scoops had the handle in contact with the ice. Ensure that ice scoops are stored in one of the manner listed below. The ice scoops were moved during the inspection. 
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to not be working properly. The sanitizer concentration was testing at 0 ppm. Facility was able to repair the dish machine to working order during the inspection. Ensure that the dish machine is regularly checked to ensure it is working at the proper concentration. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed a shelf in the rear of the facility to have an accumulation of sugar. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned often as necessary to maintain free of accumulation of debris. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service items being stored on top of soda syrup lines with the food contact surface up. Ensure that single service is stored in a manner that prevents the contamination of the food surfaces. Single service were moved and inverted during the inspection. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed personal coats and bags being stored on top of bulk product, as well as the soda syrup area. Ensure that employee areas are designated for storage to prevent cross contamination. Items moved during the inspection. 
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to have a spray bottle, with a white liquid in it, at the utility sink. The bottle was not labeled. Bottle was identified as degreaser and labeled during the inspection. Ensure all chemcials in the facility are properly labeled to prevent accidental misuse or contamination of surfaces. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed excessively soiled cardboard, with a microwave resting on it, on top a cooler in the kitchen. Ensure that when using cardboard within the facility that it is discarded at the end of the day. The soiled cardboard being maintained in the facility could lead to pest issues in the future. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed knives being stored in a pan below a table top. Some of the knives were soiled, while other were clean. It was noted that all were intended to be clean, but food had since fallen into the container. Ensure that utensils are stored in a manner that prevents them from being contaminated. They were placed into the dish area to be cleaned.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
There was a metal single service container being reused on the table in the kitchen. While this has been allowed within the facility, the container was noted to have rust on it. This is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that if reusing approved single-service articles that they are discarded when they are in disrepair or no longer able to be adequately cleaned.  
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a spray bottle of chemicals with tape around it, but no notable label. Owner stated it was degreaser and labeled the bottle as such. Ensure that all chemicals within the facility are labeled to ensure that they are not misused. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed egg cartons, without eggs in them, to be being stored on top of the double door cooler in the kitchen. Eggs contain the majority of their pathogens on the exterior of the eggs, thusly the egg carton should be disposed of promptly following use. Egg cartons discarded during the inspection. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed a metal container, below a table, that contained sugar. The container was unlabeled and did not have a lid provided to protect the sugar inside. Ensure that a lid is provided to protect the food from potentials of cross contamination. 
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine testing at 0 ppm for Cl. Owner moved the sanitizer bucket to an angle to allow the use of the rest of the sanitizer in the bucket, since there was a low amount left. Dish machine tested at 100 ppm following this. Ensure sanitizers are regularly monitored so the proper concentration of solution is being used during the dish washing process. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the top of the dish machine to have an excessive accumulation of grease. Ensure that this area is regularly cleaned to prevent potentials for cross contamination of the clean dishes.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings in the dry storage area on two separate shelves. There were mouse traps noted in this area as well, but the amount of dropping was significant. Owner contacting Sentinel today. Ensure that this area is thoroughly cleaned to continue pest monitoring and that any extra needed measures are taken. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a spray bottle at the mop sink that was unlableled. The owner was allowed to label it during the inspeciton with "bleach water". Ensure that all chemical bottles are labeled with what they contain to prevent potentials for cross contamination. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances. {

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed an employee to use the in-use ladle to taste the food being created in the wok. Ladle was about to be returned to the food, event was stopped by inspector. See violation #s 20 and 16 as well. Ladle was removed for wash, rinse, and sanitizing.  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-820a Observed an operator attempting to wash, rinse, and sanitize a soiled ladle without properly washing or rinsing the utensils. Discussed the process for proper washing of soiled utensils. Facility should insure staff has knowledge of proper washing procedures.  For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-820d Observed a soiled ladle to be rinsed in the three compartment sink and not moved through the proper wash, rinse, and sanitizing procedures. Ladle was removed from service. Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed the clean utensils in a plastic container that contained debris as well. Store clean untensils in a manner that prevents potentials cross-contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed a bulk container of take-home containers to be stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Stored off the floor during the inspection.  Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: 750-1120 The facility was finally able to produce hot water from these faucets. Aerator was cleaned and water began flowing freely. The basement bathrooms barely have running water available. Hot and cold water are trickling out of the faucet. The facility believes the water pipes to this lower portion of the facility have frozen. Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Observed several coats and sweaters on the dry storage shelves in the dry storage closet. Shelving is a mix of food and office items. See that shelving is organized into only food and only office. Store personal items on office shelves.  Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment: 750-100 Observed a dented can of Nestle Carnation Evaporated Milk stored on the dry storage shelves. Can was dented along the bottom seam. Can was discarded during the inspection. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed improper cooling of pork and fried rice. Pork was observed covered at 76F within the prep cooler. Food was left uncovered and time was indicated on the food during the inspection. Also, two large tubs of fried rice are observed resting on the counter at 123F. No time was indicated on the food. Rice was indicated as being too hot to put into the cooler. Later, rice was indicated as going to be used for dinner. Leave rice hot between food service or store in a shallow pan, uncovered, and with time indicated on the packaging. See notes on cooling in General Comments section. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed the bottom of containers holding green onions and another holding lemons to be resting on top of cabbage in the mini cooler. Another container of veggies is observed with the bottom resting on sliced cucumber in this same cooler. Cease allowing the bottom of one container to touch food in another container. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed employee touch pork in the preparation cooler (with bare hands) to check the temperature. Cease using bare hands to check temperatures of foods.   Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510d Observed several employees improperly washing their hands. Hands are observed being washed with clean hands used to turn off faucet and then grab a paper towel. During the inspection, discussed handwashing. Cease using clean hand to turn off faucet. Use a barrier. To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed a half eaten container of cheesy potatoes on top of clean equipment over the wait area in the kitchen. Also, observed a McDonald's coffee cup over the prep cooler on the cook corner. Food was discarded during the inspection. Cease allowing personal foods to rest on surfaces with restaurant equipment and over food. Store personal drinks in such a manner as to not contaminate anything should a spill occur. Also, store coffee cups and other containers by the handsink so that hands may be washed after taking a drink. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a Observed facility using metal cans and grocery sacks to hold cut vegetables. Cease using metal and non-food grade plastics to hold foods. The metal can rust or have physical pieces fall into food. Cease reusing metal and grocery sacks. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Tables are being wiped down with spray bottle of sanitizer and wet wiping cloth. When cleaning make sure that sani-buckets and cloths are used OR spray bottles and paper toweling is used. Cloths should be stored in sanitizing solution between uses. Paper towels should be used and then discarded. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the wire metal shelf by the preparation cooler to be thickly coated with grease and food debris. Clean the shelf.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the floor underneath the back shelf storage to be soiled with dust and crumbs. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the plumbing and the wall around and behind the wok to be soiled with food splash and grease. Clean the walls and attached plumbing. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-1390 Observed the mop head to be stored on the floor by the backdoor. Invert mop or hang so that mop can properly drip dry. Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Single use forks are stored with handles and times mixed. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Face single use utensils and clean out container holding single use portion cups.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floor under the black shelves is soiled. Also floor in difficult to reach areas has some accumulated soil. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors maintain clean.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
Inspector was unable to locate a thermometer in the chest freezer in the store room.
Provide thermometer for each refrigeration unit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
Observed that the table used to store clean cooking pans is constructed of wood, and the coating has eroded over time on the surface. Recoat table so as to be smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
Observed that the wall behind the grille has some grease splatter from the wok.
Clean this wall as necessary.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.
Observed that a ceiling tile over the dish machine has been repaired with duct tape. Repair ceiling tile with a more durable material, so as to be easily cleanable.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
Observed that the damp mop was not hung up between uses.
Store mop hanging upright so as to promote air drying.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:

750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  
Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed that the cold-side faucet at the 3 compartment sink was not working properly. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.
Repair faucet at 3 compartment sink.
**NOTE** = Owner was repairing faucet during inspection.

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed that there are two ceiling tiles in the kitchen near the dish area that are sagging from the ceiling. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
Repair the ceiling tiles in the kitchen.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 1) Observed two containers of cooked chicken cooling in the refrigerator to be 92F and 95F. Kitchen cook stated the chicken had only been in the refrigerator for 10 minutes and out of temperature control for less than 30 minutes. 2) Observed a tray of fried chicken to be on the counter top at 85F. Kitchen cook stated the food had been out for one hour. Handout on proper cooling given. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
